title: adaptive-lint-scheduler-and-dep-staleness-badge
author: Priya Nair
description: Overview: introduce an adaptive lint scheduler that reduces CI waste by routing lint jobs into three tiers (quick, focused, full) based on a hot-file score, touched path cardinality, and a historical flake index. Add a dependency-staleness badge that annotates PRs with a human-friendly score and a short remediation hint; the badge is produced by a low-footprint indexer that runs as a presubmit step in advisory mode by default. This change modularizes workflow templates, replaces a monolithic lint job with a scheduler hook, and adds telemetry to track shard efficiency and dep churn. Rollout: advisory for 14 days, opt-in by team via .github/ci/policy.yaml. Motivation: flakey long lint runs and blanket full-lint on large refactors consume CI slots and increase queue latency. The scheduler preserves correctness (full tier still available) while accelerating common small changes.

review_comments: Jamal Ahmed: Scheduler looks good; please document the fallthrough rule when path analysis fails.
Priya Nair (author): Fallthrough set to 'full' with a safety cap; added details to README and unit tests.
Renee Park: Can we expose a per-team opt-out label so owners can opt-out without editing policy files?

Samir Gupta: The dep indexer should not block merges in advisory mode; confirm badge failures don't fail presubmit.
Priya Nair (author): Advisory mode emits ci.dep_badge.status metric and never blocks merges by default; gating can be enabled later via policy.
release_notes: Add adaptive lint scheduler that splits lint into quick/focused/full tiers using hot-file scoring and historical flake signals; introduce dep-staleness badge (advisory by default) that surfaces dependency age and quick remediation hints on PRs; modular CI templates and opt-in per-team controls. Observability: ci.scheduler.tier_count and ci.dep_staleness.score metrics added. Default rollout: advisory for two weeks, then review metrics for gating decision.
